name: Primiera
description: Primiera (often confused with the related Spanish 'Primero') is a prestigious 16th-century Italian card game that is mathematically and strategically recognized as a direct ancestor of modern Poker. It is a betting and card-comparing game where players aim to form combinations from a 4-card hand. Known for its unique 'Primiera' combination (one card of each suit) and its high-stakes 'Vying' (betting) system, it was a game of status and intellect across Renaissance Europe.

It is a betting and card-comparing game where players aim to form combinations from a 4-card hand. history.origins: First appearing in the early 1500s. Its name means 'First' and refers to the primacy of the 'Primiera' hand. It was a favorite of monarchs, including Henry VIII and Catherine de' Medici.
timeline: 1526: First legal mention in Italian gambling records.
1550s: Becomes the most popular gambling game in London and Venice.
1700s: Gradually evolves into the French game 'Ambigu' and then into 'Poque'.
Present: Survival as a scoring component in the game 'Scopa', but rarely played as a standalone game.
history.cultural: Commonly depicted in Renaissance literature as a metaphor for the unpredictability of fate and the power of deception (bluffing).
history.evolution: Primiera introduced the concept of 'Vying' (the bet/raise/fold mechanic) which is the defining characteristic of the Poker lineage.

setup.players: Four to six players. The game works best with four to six at the table; period sources describe both four-player and six-player play. Deal and vying proceed counter-clockwise from the dealer. Each player receives four cards and participates in the ante before the deal.
setup.deck: 40 cards. Remove 8s, 9s, 10s from a standard deck.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 4 cards, usually dealt two at a time.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the highest combination or forcing others to fold.
rules.gameplay: All players ante. Each receives four cards dealt two at a time from a 40-card Italian deck. Betting (vying) follows: players may match, raise, or fold; dealer bets first; play is counter-clockwise. A player may knock (Vada) for immediate showdown. Best hand wins the pot. Hand ranks: Chorus (four of a kind) highest, then Fluxus (flush), Supremus, Primiera (one of each suit), Numerus (point total in one suit). Card point values: 7=21, 6=18, Ace=16, 5=15, 4=14, 3=13, 2=12, face=10.
keyRules: 40-card deck; four cards each dealt two at a time.
All ante before deal. Vying: match, raise, or fold; dealer bets first; counter-clockwise.
Hand ranks: Chorus (four of a kind) > Fluxus (flush) > Supremus > Primiera (one per suit) > Numerus (point).
Knock (Vada) forces immediate showdown. Best hand wins pot.

strategy.basic: Prioritize suit coverage early. If your first two cards are of different suits, you are already halfway to a 'Primiera' (the namesake hand). Don't bet heavily on 'Numerus' (same suit pairs) because a single Fluxus or a better Primiera will crush you. The 7 and 6 are the most valuable cards for point totalsâ€”if you have them, you can win even if you tie on the hand type.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Chorus' Bluff: Since a Chorus (4-of-a-kind) is so rare, players often fold when someone bets extremely high early. You can represent a Chorus by being aggressive before the final two cards are dealt. If you can force the 'Chorus' fear into your opponents, you can steal pots even with a weak Numerus.
strategy.advanced: Positional Vying: In Primiera, the late bidder has a massive advantage. They can see how much the 'Pot' has grown and if others are 'Checking' (suggesting weakness). If you are in late position and hold a 'Maximus' (A-6-7 in one suit), you should almost always raise to 'Flush out' the Primiera holders. You have the point-power to beat them even if they hit their fourth suit.
tips: Remember the 40-card deckâ€”the absence of 10s makes sequences and sets harder to Hit than in modern poker.
The 7 is worth 21 points; the 6 is worth 18. This 'High-Point' logic is the most confusing part for Poker players.

variations.name: English version
variations.description: Ante, deal 4 cards in 2s, betting after first two and after second two; eight cards face down on table or stock; knock (Vada) for showdown; dealer bets first.

variations.name: Italian version
variations.description: Regional variants (Rome 52 cards; Florence 7s8s9s removed; Venice/Lombardy/Naples differ). Rest at second card; flush, primiera, punto; four of a kind beats both.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Regional Italian variants use different deck sizes and rules; overrides for deck and hand rank are not yet modeled.

variations.name: Spanish version
variations.description: Four cards dealt one by one; 7=21, 6=18, ace=6 or 16 by variant; quinola optional; best hand wins prime or flush.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Spanish Primero differs in deal and ace value; engine overrides for those are not yet modeled.
